2L.10 Confession and supplication to God required before God will release a nation from enemy infliction or captivity.

precepts.text: When the blessing and the curse are come upon them and they return to the Most High among the nations, he promises to gather them from all the peoples where he scattered them, even from the outmost parts of heaven, the very promise Nehemiah pleads.
precepts.point: This is Nehemiah quoting Deuteronomy 28, holding the Most High to what Moses had already taught in the wilderness, both the scattering and the gathering.
precepts.why:
Nehemiah confesses that Israel “have not kept the commandments, nor the statutes, nor the judgments, which thou commandedst thy servant Moses”, and then pleads the word the Most High gave Moses: “If ye transgress, I will scatter you abroad among the nations: But if ye turn unto me, and keep my commandments, and do them; though there were of you cast out unto the uttermost part of the heaven, yet will I gather them from thence”.

This is that promise. Moses said that when “the blessing and the curse” have come upon them and they “call them to mind among all the nations, whither the Lord thy God hath driven thee, And shalt return unto the Lord thy God, and shalt obey his voice according to all that I command thee this day”, then “the Lord thy God will turn thy captivity, and have compassion upon thee, and will return and gather thee from all the nations, whither the Lord thy God hath scattered thee. If any of thine be driven out unto the outmost parts of heaven, from thence will the Lord thy God gather thee”.

Nehemiah is holding the Most High to what Moses had already taught in the wilderness, both the scattering and the gathering. The curse for transgressing is scattering among the nations; the promise for turning and keeping the commandments is gathering from the outmost parts of heaven to the place he has chosen to set his name. Nehemiah's prayer rests on that word.

moments.label: God's People Need Charity, Healing & Trust

points: Let thine ear now be attentive, and thine eyes open, that thou mayest hear the prayer of thy servant, which I pray before thee now, day and night, for the children of Israel thy servants, and confess the sins of the children of Israel, which we have sinned against thee: both I and my father's house have sinned. What did Nehemiah do at that point? He took responsibility, and he also suffered what they suffered as well. He included himself in it. He considered, I am not just praying and saying the people sinned, I myself was in error, my whole house is in error. Consider that as a leader.

note.label: God's People Need Charity, Healing & Trust

points: These are the words of Nehemiah the son of Hachaliah. In the month Chisleu, in the twentieth year, as he was in the palace, Hanani one of his brethren comes with certain men of Judah, and Nehemiah asks concerning the Jews that had escaped the captivity and concerning Jerusalem.
They tell him the remnant left of the captivity in the province are in great affliction and reproach, the wall of Jerusalem is broken down, and its gates are burned with fire.
When Nehemiah hears these words he sits down, weeps, mourns certain days, and fasts and prays before the God of heaven.
He beseeches the Lord God of heaven, the great and terrible God that keeps covenant and mercy for them that love him and keep his commandments, that his ear would be attentive and his eyes open.

He asks that the Most High hear the prayer he prays day and night for the children of Israel, and he confesses the sins of the children of Israel which they have sinned, both himself and his father's house.
He confesses they have dealt very corruptly and not kept the commandments, statutes, or judgments the Most High commanded his servant Moses.

He pleads the word the Most High commanded Moses, that if they transgress he will scatter them abroad among the nations, but if they turn and keep his commandments and do them, though they were cast out to the uttermost part of heaven, he will gather them from thence and bring them to the place he has chosen to set his name.

These are the servants and the people whom the Most High has redeemed by his great power and strong hand, and Nehemiah asks that the Lord's ear be attentive to the prayer of his servant and of the servants who desire to fear his name.

He asks the Most High to prosper his servant this day and grant him mercy in the sight of this man, for he was the king's cupbearer, whose job was to serve the wine and keep a joyous countenance before the king.
